clue.text: Caught by man from the FBI, I would become worried

definitions.note: past tense verb: worried at, fussed with restlessly

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it, so the FBI man's letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: a FED is American slang for a federal agent, such as one from the FBI
I'd is the contraction of I would
to get can mean to become, as in get angry

explanation.surface: An FBI agent arrests someone, who grows anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught by' is the container signal: the FBI man holds the rest. 'Worried' is a verb here, as in worrying at something with the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: To fidget is to fiddle restlessly, much as one worries at something with the fingers.

clue.text: Invention suitable for investment by government law officers

indicators.note: investment means being clothed or surrounded, so suitable wraps round the officers

parts.note: fit means suitable
G-men are FBI agents, government men

explanation.surface: An idea seems right for federal agents to put money into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' suggests finance but here means clothing or surrounding, the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment is something made up by the imagination.

clue.text: Without uttering a word, cast cause a sensation

parts.note: dumb means silent, saying nothing
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: A silent troupe of actors makes a big impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a group of actors but means shaped in a mould, FOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: To dumbfound is to astonish, leaving someone amazed.

clue.text: English sailors wearing duck that's indestructible

indicators.note: the duck is wearing the sailors, meaning they sit inside it

parts.note: a teal is a small duck
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: English seamen in tough canvas trousers that never wear out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' is the container signal: the duck has the sailors on it. 'Duck' could be a cricket score or a dodge, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal lasts for ever and cannot be destroyed.

clue.text: Employed the former King Edward

parts.note: ex means former
ER is the cipher of a monarch, here Edwardus Rex
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A dethroned king finds work again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Exerted means applied or brought into use, as with effort or influence.

clue.text: Fill in with a transposition that's cheerful here

indicators.note: a transposition swaps the order of parts, so a piece of the phrase is shifted to the other end

parts.note: in British slang to fill someone in is to beat them up

explanation.surface: Instructions for completing a puzzle by swapping parts round to produce something jolly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fill in' is British slang for assault, so it means BEAT UP; transposing the two halves moves UP to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat describes an optimistic, positive mood.

clue.text: Moving around, the witnesses are, in court

indicators.note: moving shifts the letters of around the into a new order

explanation.surface: Witnesses shuffle about the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of AROUND THE gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Witnesses testify sworn to tell the truth, bound by a legal promise.

clue.text: The royal family takes the biscuit

definitions.meaning: the dynasty that ruled France and Spain
a chocolate sandwich biscuit sold in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: Bourbon names the French royal house and also a British chocolate-cream biscuit.

clue.text: He's not paid initially as much as the experts usually receive

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word from as to receive

explanation.surface: An unpaid man gets nearly what professionals normally earn.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur takes part for love rather than payment.

clue.text: So I looked sharp and broke my diet with glee

indicators.note: the words my diet and glee are broken up and their letters put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A dieter gleefully breaks their regime and turns keen-eyed.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of MY DIET and GLEE gives the hyphenated adjective; 'So I looked sharp' is the speaker describing themself.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimlet is a sharp boring tool, so a gimlet-eyed person has a piercing, keen stare.

clue.text: Tree father planted in America

indicators.note: planted in means put inside, so father's letters go inside America's

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States of America
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad sets a sapling into American soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a poisonous tropical Asian tree of the fig family.

clue.text: A change for the better, infernal brat

indicators.note: a change rearranges the letters of better and infernal into a new order

explanation.surface: A badly behaved child is said to have improved, though still hellish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' signals the anagram of BETTER INFERNAL; 'A' and 'for the' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: An enfant terrible is a French phrase for a precocious troublemaker, literally a terrible child.

clue.text: All abroad were first made to look untidy

parts.note: tous is French for all, abroad meaning in a foreign tongue
led means were first, as runners in front

explanation.surface: Travellers who led the way all ended up dishevelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' tells you to use a foreign word: French TOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tousled hair or clothing has been rumpled into disorder.

clue.text: Monstrous egoism — the Scots revel in it

indicators.note: monstrous means grotesquely misshapen, so egoism and the are reshaped

explanation.surface: Dreadful self-regard is the life and soul of a Scottish party.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'the' after the dash, which supplies THE for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightsome reel is a lively Scottish country dance for eight people.

clue.text: Washing.. makes city wet, presumably

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
something wet is presumably not dry, coined here as un-dry

explanation.surface: Doing the washing soaks a whole city.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful UNDRY, a made-up opposite of dry, is flagged by 'presumably'.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry is the clothes and linen being washed.

clue.text: Leaving legendary king without aspiration, in' deep trouble

indicators.note: in places the shortened king inside the jumbled letters
deep trouble: the word deep is troubled, its letters stirred
without means losing, so the breathy letter is dropped

parts.note: Arthur is the legendary king of Camelot
H is the aspirate, a breathy sound

explanation.surface: A mythical king's going leaves him in serious difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTUR (Arthur without H) goes inside DEPE, an anagram of 'deep' signalled by 'trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: A departure is an act of going away.

clue.text: Gentleman lay low, in the past, without money

parts.note: to lie low is to hide, so lay low means hid

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the past wraps round money

parts.note: ago means in the past
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A gentleman once hid away, broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: AGO goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a Spanish nobleman of the lower ranks.

clue.text: Drive up: the motorway, going… up to college

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the motorway is turned round

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London

indicators.note: going here means turning about, so the second up is read backwards

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A driver heads north on the motorway towards university.
explanation.walkthrough: MI reversed gives IM, UP reversed gives PU, then LSE. The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is an urge or driving force.

clue.text: Leave an orchestra playing

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article a
a band is a group of musicians
on means taking place, being performed

explanation.surface: A musician quits mid-performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to desert or forsake.

clue.text: The craft is a cutter.

definitions.meaning: an aircraft, specifically a helicopter, in slang
a tool for cutting, like an axe or cleaver

explanation.definitionFit: Chopper is slang for a helicopter, and also a heavy blade for hacking meat or wood.

clue.text: It makes you laugh when officer turns up interrupting work …

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the officer sits inside work

parts.note: a chore is a piece of work

indicators.note: in a down entry turns up reverses the officer's letters

parts.note: Lt is lieutenant

explanation.surface: A joke when an officer arrives and disturbs the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' looks like arrives; in a down clue it reverses LT.
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful chuckle.

clue.text: … Harry's work on papers

definitions.note: the definition is harry, the 's being is linking it to the wordplay

parts.note: op is opus, a work
the press is the newspapers

explanation.surface: Continuing the laugh: Harry's latest work is in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name, but it is the verb meaning harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass or persecute persistently.

clue.text: Fluster, shattering calm

indicators.note: shattering breaks the word fluster to pieces to be reassembled

explanation.surface: Agitation destroys composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Restful means peaceful and soothing.

clue.text: French dressing?

parts.note: not a salad dressing but a surgical dressing named after the French capital

explanation.definitionFit: This white gypsum paste sets hard to make casts for broken limbs, a kind of medical dressing linked by name with France.

clue.text: 11 not out, hurt, needs runners, to go on

indicators.note: not means without, so these letters are taken away from the other answer

parts.note: the answer to clue 11 across
the word out, hurt meaning damaged, has its three letters jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricketer on eleven not out, though injured, needs runners to continue batting.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove TOU (the word 'out' jumbled, 'hurt' being the signal) from the answer to 11. The cricket surface: an injured batsman could have a runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled moves on runners, so it cannot travel without them.

clue.text: Not working — they nearly all strike without premeditation

parts.note: a machine that is not working is off

indicators.note: nearly all of the word they means losing its final letter

parts.note: to cuff is to strike with the hand

explanation.surface: Workers down tools as almost everyone walks out on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: The industrial picture of a strike misleads: 'strike' means hit, giving CUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done off the cuff is improvised, spoken without preparation.

clue.text: Meeting helping to oppose ancestor worship

indicators.note: a helping is a portion, so a portion of the following words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A gathering assisting in resisting the veneration of forebears.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'opposE ANCEstor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a sitting at which people try to contact the dead.

clue.text: One of the empty houses on the coast that people, pick up for nothing

definitions.text: One of the empty houses on the coast that people, pick up for nothing

parts.words: One of the empty houses on the coast that people, pick up for nothing
parts.note: the surface suggests free seaside property; really a vacated shell home of a sea creature found on the beach

explanation.definitionFit: A mollusc's discarded home lies on the beach for anyone to collect free.
